faq.lockProtects.q: What does the passcode lock protect, and what doesn't it?
faq.lockProtects.a: Once locked, people who pick up your device see only the lock screen. It locks after the time you pick, and when you leave the app if you turn that on; inside a Board program it can wait up to 15 minutes longer. Each tab and window locks and unlocks on its own; Lock now locks them all. It doesn't encrypt your sign-in: someone who can read this browser's storage (developer tools, malware, a rooted phone) can still use it. The phone may show a preview of the Hub in its app switcher. Your account on other devices is not affected.
faq.lockScope.q: Does the passcode follow me to other tabs and browsers, and what removes it?
faq.lockScope.a: The lock is for this browser only. Each tab and window locks on its own; new tabs and reloads ask for the passcode. Signing out keeps the passcode on this browser; to remove it, use Remove passcode or Forget this browser. After you sign in again, the Hub still asks for it. Clearing this site's data removes the lock and signs you out of the Hub here. Notices already shown on this device stay there.
faq.removeLocal.q: What does Remove all local data do?
faq.removeLocal.a: The Hub signs you out: it tries to end this browser's session and its agent sign-in on the server, and always clears the sign-in on this device. Then it forgets everything it keeps in this browser: saved settings, layouts, drafts and the changes it is tracking, for every account that signed in here. Your account, your computers and your data on the server stay as they are. It only runs while this is the only Hoody Hub tab open in this browser.
faq.emailChange.q: What happens when I change my email address?
faq.emailChange.a: The Hub tries to send a confirm link to the new address. It works for 24 hours at most: a newer request replaces it, some account changes cancel it, and if the address can't be used no link is sent. Your email changes only when you open it. The Hub also tries to send your current address a notice, and after the change a link to undo it for 7 days. Until the undo period ends you can't change it again. You need your current password, and your two-step code if it is on; if the account has no password, set one first.
faq.endSession.q: What happens when I end a sign-in session?
faq.endSession.a: Ending a session signs that browser or device out; it can sign in again. End all other sessions signs out every browser and device except this one. Ending a session doesn't delete the API keys made there. Each row shows when it was last seen, what it signed in with and how many API keys were made there, so you can end one you do not recognise.
faq.twoStep.a: Two-step sign-in asks for a code from your authenticator app, or a backup code, on every sign-in, so a password alone is not enough. Backup codes are shown once and each works one time. When it is on, a separate switch also asks for a code when you create an API key or change its access settings (permissions, realms, expiry, allowed addresses), even to narrow them. Turning it off lets your password alone sign in again and signs out every other session.
faq.checkAgain.q: What do Check again and Stop tracking mean on a change that may have gone through?
faq.checkAgain.a: When the Hub can't tell whether a change went through, it keeps a note instead of calling it done or failed. Check again reads your account again to see whether the change is there; if it still can't tell, the note stays. Stop tracking makes the Hub stop following the change. It doesn't undo the change or mark it as failed, and doing the change again may apply it twice. For a password change, signing in again shows which password works.
faq.agentDays.q: What does the number of days for my agent set?
faq.agentDays.a: It is how long your agent stays signed in from this browser. Enter a whole number from 1 to 365. A new value applies the next time the agent's sign-in is renewed. It is saved for this browser only.
